title: The Stone That Chose to Remain

features.name: bedrock-choice
features.desc-on-touch: here is the stone that decided not to move. it could have become river-worn, become dust, become earth. it chose instead to know itself completely. you can feel its refusal and its peace.

features.name: stasis-pool
features.desc-on-touch: water that has stopped moving, pooled against stone, teaching itself that going nowhere is also a kind of purpose. the stone's reflection here is unchanging.

features.name: pressure-archive
features.desc-on-touch: layers of time pressed into the stone without sound. each layer is a year, a season, a moment the stone could have moved but chose not to. the pressure is a record of refusal.

features.name: weight-testimony
features.desc-on-touch: the archive here is pressed into matter itself. words were not needed. the stone speaks through gravity, through the force of its own choosing to rest.

reverie.title: REVERIE — touching what does not move
narr: you find katita kneeling beside this stone in the deep
red country where bedrock answers. she's pressing her palm
against it, and leif is there too, recording the sound of
stone that chose not to sing. they're both crying, quietly,
at the beauty of a thing that stayed put. the earth here
keeps its arguments inside. you join them, and time stops.

inscription: the bedrock rests from thinking and discovers that it was never arguing at all

file.name: Stone_Testimony_Deep_Archive.mp3
file.note: recordings of the deep red earth, the sound of stone not moving, Leif's voice thin and amazed, saying: it chose. it chose to stay.

exits.label: back up through the floors where argument has not yet begun
toward stone that learned to speak after long refusal
into the deepest red where pressure becomes poetry
